title: Allison Stanger named a 2026–27 Berlin Prize Fellow
gist: SFI External Professor Allison Stanger has won a 2026-27 Berlin Prize to research 'Democracy in the Age of Cryptocurrency', arguing the rules for global digital currencies are currently being written by industry insiders and fragmented national regulators rather than the ordinary citizens who bear most of the risk. Her project tests whether citizens' assemblies -- already used for climate policy and constitutional reform -- could produce transparent, accountable digital currency rules resistant to industry influence, building toward her Yale University Press book Who Elected Big Tech? due March 2027.

insights.claim: The rules for global digital currencies are currently being written by industry insiders and fragmented national regulators -- that is, by everyone except the ordinary citizens who bear most of the risk.
insights.speaker: @sfiscience
insights.so_what: Frames the coming political attack line on crypto regulation: legitimacy rather than technical risk, which points toward retail-protection rules rather than prudential ones.
insights.quote: The rules for global digital currencies are currently being written by industry insiders and fragmented national regulators — everyone, in other words, except ordinary citizens, who bear most of the risk.

insights.claim: Cryptocurrency as currently implemented risks becoming a digital Wild West in which sophisticated actors profit while ordinary investors bear the risk, threatening democratic accountability.
insights.speaker: @sfiscience
insights.so_what: An academic framing that maps directly onto consumer-protection enforcement -- the argument regulators cite when restricting retail crypto distribution.

insights.claim: Cryptocurrency poses a distinctive governance problem because it operates beyond national borders and no single country controls it, making unilateral national regulation structurally inadequate.
insights.speaker: @sfiscience
insights.so_what: Regulatory arbitrage persists until a supranational mechanism exists -- jurisdiction shopping remains a live feature of crypto business models for now.

insights.claim: Money should be understood as a mirror of the political institutions behind it rather than as a neutral technology, so debates about digital currency design are debates about political authority.
insights.speaker: @sfiscience
insights.so_what: A useful lens for reading CBDC and stablecoin policy fights as contests over institutional control, not payments efficiency.
insights.quote: Money has never been just a technology — it’s a mirror of the political institutions behind it
insights.locator: Money has never been just a technology

themes.theme: Citizens' assemblies as a regulatory mechanism

insights.claim: Citizens' assemblies -- groups of ordinary people convened to address complex policy questions -- have already shown they can tackle remarkably technical questions from climate policy to constitutional reform, and are being tested as a route to writing digital currency rules.
insights.speaker: @sfiscience
insights.so_what: A plausible new institutional channel for crypto rulemaking that would sideline industry lobbying -- worth tracking as a tail risk to incumbent regulatory capture.
insights.locator: It pairs a historical analysis of money

insights.claim: The research design pairs a historical analysis of money from ancient coins to modern cryptocurrencies with an institutional-design study, treating crypto as the latest stage in a long institutional sequence rather than a discontinuity.
insights.speaker: @sfiscience
insights.so_what: Historical-continuity framings tend to produce regulate-like-money conclusions rather than novel-asset-class ones -- a directional hint for policy output.
insights.locator: It pairs a historical analysis of money

insights.claim: Stanger's work builds toward a forthcoming Yale University Press book, Who Elected Big Tech?, available in March 2027, extending the democratic-accountability critique from crypto to technology platforms generally.
insights.speaker: @sfiscience
insights.so_what: A dated catalyst for renewed platform-accountability discourse ahead of any 2027 regulatory cycle.
